A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpikingBrain and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. The complete documents, including v3's Appendix A, support reliable matching across reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, training and inference measurements, and spiking experiments, including Tables 1–6 and Figures 6–10.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a six-task LongBench comparison in Appendix A.4, Table 5.

M1.justification: The 7B and 76B architectures, attention configurations, MoE upcycling, adaptive-threshold spiking, coding variants and conversion pipeline remain unchanged. Revised diagrams and consolidated equations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v3 adds six-task LongBench evaluation, including previously unreported HotpotQA, NarrativeQA, TREC, MultiNews and Qasper evaluations alongside TriviaQA, already represented as TrQ. This substantially broadens practical long-context task coverage beyond the retained general benchmarks and QuALITY.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparator membership. The added LongBench comparison uses Jamba, Qwen2.5 and Mixtral, all already compared against SpikingBrain-76B in v2 Table 2; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: The new LongBench protocol evaluates SpikingBrain-76B after stage-2 SFT and truncates prompts to 32k because of baseline positional-embedding limits. Existing training budgets, evaluation frameworks and latency procedures are retained.

E4.justification: The floating-point versus spiking comparison, spike-distribution analysis, coding visualizations and hardware-energy estimates are retained. LongBench adds benchmark evaluation rather than an ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging sequence-parallel TTFT measurements over 10 runs, in v2 Table 4 and v3 Table 6. No new seed information, uncertainty intervals or significance-testing procedures appear.

E6.justification: v3 Table 5 adds a substantive six-task LongBench results block with mixed rankings: SpikingBrain-76B scores 50.00 versus Qwen2.5's 57.62 on HotpotQA, but 90.84 versus 85.92 on TriviaQA. These are newly reported results under the added protocol; existing benchmark, latency, spiking and energy values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The attention mathematics, MoE rescaling, spiking definitions and energy calculation are retained. For example, v2 Equations 19–22 are consolidated into v3 Equation 18 and accompanying prose without changing the mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The core contributions and claims remain conversion-based 7B/76B models, hybrid attention and spiking efficiency, competitive performance, and large-scale MetaX feasibility. Abstract editing and additional LongBench support do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds the interpretation that SpikingBrain-76B remains competitive on practical LongBench tasks while using only four global softmax-attention layers. Existing qualifications about architectural performance gaps, alignment data and specialized asynchronous hardware remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 supplies reproducibility information for the added LongBench experiment: the stage-2 SFT checkpoint and 32k prompt-truncation rule. Previously documented architecture parameters, calibration settings, hardware, CPU deployment details and code access are retained or relocated.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bai et al. (2024), LongBench. The earlier referenced works are retained; author-year citation formatting and expanded bibliographic metadata account for the other reference changes, without substantially revising research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes experimental documentation into Appendix A.1–A.7, covering benchmarks, models, instruct results, efficiency tables, CPU deployment and spike visualization. Main-text explanations are condensed, chat terminology becomes instruct terminology, and the abstract and authorship text are edited.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and the CPU inference diagram are extensively redrawn. Existing speed plots are placed side by side, several tables and the firing-map figure move to the appendix, the TTFT table is transposed, and a new LongBench table is added.

improvement.justification: The added LongBench comparison provides useful additional empirical support for practical long-context use while preserving the earlier results. The gain is limited to the stage-2 SFT 76B model with 32k-truncated prompts; the extensive diagram and document restructuring mainly changes presentation.
